verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The Lean's core is cut out by the same two similarity coordinates, but three things differ. (i) coreDomain is a space-time set over all t < 1, not the time slice C_τ; unfolding it at fixed t gives exactly a slice of C_τ's shape, so this one is pure packaging. (ii) The radial cap is the strict Λ·X ∈ (-20,20), i.e. 0 ≤ X < X_c with X_c = 20/Λ (X = s/q ≥ 0 automatically, s = r^2/2), where the paper closes the interval at X_c; open versus closed. (iii) The η cap is |η| < 11/10, which is no restriction at all: eta_sq_lt_one gives |η| < 1 at every point with τ > 0, so the Lean's "core" reaches the endpoints η → ±1, whereas the paper fixes η_c < 1 precisely to stay away from them — that is the hypothesis under which q ≍ τ, and hence under which the next two displays hold. In NaturalCore the enlarged set is used only as an open domain of smoothness and of the divergence identity (coreVelocity_contDiffOn, coreVelocity_divergence, exists_natural_core), where enlarging it is harmless; no declaration was found that imposes a cap η_c < 1 on a core region.
